metaData.title: DynoSim: Simulating the Pareto Frontier
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: DynoSim is a discrete-event simulation of the NVIDIA Dynamo serving stack that enables fast, faithful exploration of the deployment configuration Pareto frontier before committing GPU time.
metaData.summary: DynoSim is a workload-driven discrete-event simulator for the NVIDIA Dynamo LLM serving stack. It models the full inference pipeline—scheduler, router, planner, KV cache manager—on a single virtual timeline, using measured engine forward-pass timing from AIConfigurator. This allows developers to sweep thousands of deployment configurations (tensor-parallel shape, worker counts, routing policy, autoscaling settings, etc.) in seconds rather than hours of real GPU time. The simulator achieves ~1,500x speedup over real time on a MacBook Air. The article demonstrates DynoSim's utility through concrete experiments: KV-aware routing improves prefix cache reuse from 0.38 to 0.44-0.45; enabling the G2 host-memory tier reduces TTFT by 19.3% at peak; and autoscaling experiments reveal optimal scaling intervals (5-10 seconds) and cold-start thresholds (~180 seconds) for a Qwen3-32B workload. The vision is to make simulation the inner loop for deployment tuning, with real clusters serving as the outer validation loop, and eventually to close the loop with continuous production re-optimization.

mainPoints.point: DynoSim enables fast, faithful simulation of the entire LLM serving stack at the forward-pass level.
mainPoints.explanation: By composing scheduler, router, planner, and KV cache manager on a single discrete-event timeline, DynoSim models complex cross-layer interactions that analytical estimates miss, achieving ~1,500x speedup over real time.

mainPoints.point: Scheduler-aware replay significantly improves TTFT prediction accuracy over pure engine timing estimates.
mainPoints.explanation: AIConfigurator provides accurate per-pass timing, but TTFT is sensitive to how requests wait, batch, and chunk under high concurrency. Adding scheduler simulation closes the gap between estimates and hardware measurements.

mainPoints.point: KV-aware routing and host-memory tiering yield measurable improvements in cache reuse and latency.
mainPoints.explanation: KV-aware routing increases prefix cache reuse from 0.38 to 0.44-0.45, reducing TTFT. Enabling the G2 host-memory tier improves mean TTFT by 19.3% at peak concurrency by reducing prefill recompute.

mainPoints.point: DynoSim enables systematic exploration of autoscaling policies, revealing optimal parameters and failure thresholds.
mainPoints.explanation: Experiments show that scaling intervals of 5-10 seconds balance responsiveness and churn, and that cold-start delays beyond ~180 seconds cause catastrophic SLA violations for a Qwen3-32B workload.

mainPoints.point: The vision is to make simulation the inner loop for continuous production optimization.
mainPoints.explanation: DynoSim can periodically sweep configurations against recent production traffic, recommending or applying reconfigurations as workload distributions drift over hours and days.

keyQuotes: DynoSim is a workload-driven discrete-event simulation of the NVIDIA Dynamo serving stack.

On an Apple M4 MacBook Air, the single-threaded Rust offline replay simulated the full 23,608-request Mooncake trace... in 2.41 seconds of wall time. The simulated serving window was 60.1 minutes, about 1,500x faster than real time.
The goal is not to replace real-cluster validation. The goal is to make that validation more focused.

A smart sweeping algorithm built on top of DynoSim would run periodically against recently-recorded production traffic, search the configuration space under the current workload distribution, and recommend (or directly apply) a reconfiguration when a materially better deployment is found.
A local improvement can shift the bottleneck somewhere else.

relatedArticles.title: Introducing Nemotron 3 Super: An Open Hybrid Mamba-Transformer MoE for Agentic Reasoning
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: NVIDIA introduces Nemotron 3 Super, a 120B hybrid Mamba-Transformer MoE model featuring a 1M context window and innovative Latent MoE architecture optimized for agentic reasoning.

relatedArticles.title: NVIDIA Ising Introduces AI-Powered Workflows to Build Fault-Tolerant Quantum Systems
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: NVIDIA introduces Ising, the first open family of AI models designed to tackle quantum computing's core challenge of qubit noise through two specialized domains: a vision-language model for automated quantum processor calibration and 3D CNN models for real-time quantum error correction decoding.

relatedArticles.title: NVIDIA Platform Delivers Lowest Token Cost Enabled by Extreme Co-Design
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: NVIDIA's performance in the MLPerf Inference v6.0 benchmarks demonstrates the efficacy of full-stack co-design, with software optimizations in TensorRT-LLM and Dynamo delivering significant throughput gains on existing Blackwell Ultra hardware.

relatedArticles.title: NVIDIA Dynamo Snapshot: Fast Startup for Inference Workloads on Kubernetes
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: NVIDIA introduces Dynamo Snapshot, a checkpoint/restore system using CRIU and cuda-checkpoint with novel optimizations to reduce inference workload cold-start times on Kubernetes from minutes to under 5 seconds.

relatedArticles.title: Slack AI: The Path to Multi-Cloud
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Slack Engineering details its multi-year journey from AWS SageMaker to a multi-cloud AI architecture on AWS Bedrock and GCP Vertex AI, driven by the need for operational efficiency, model agility, and enterprise-grade reliability.

relatedArticles.title: Building for the Rising Complexity of Agentic Systems with Extreme Co-Design
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article analyzes how agentic AI systems fundamentally change inference workload dynamics, driving extreme token consumption and latency requirements that necessitate a purpose-built, co-designed hardware and software platform like NVIDIA's Vera Rubin stack.

relatedArticles.title: Achieving Single-Digit Microsecond Latency Inference for Capital Markets
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details how NVIDIA achieves record-breaking single-digit microsecond latency for LSTM-based inference in algorithmic trading using custom CUDA kernels and hardware-specific optimizations on GH200 and Blackwell GPUs.

relatedArticles.title: Removing the Guesswork from Disaggregated Serving
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: AIConfigurator is an open-source tool by NVIDIA that optimizes LLM serving—especially disaggregated and MoE workloads—by predicting performance through primitive-level measurements instead of exhaustive GPU testing.

relatedArticles.title: Full-Stack Optimizations for Agentic Inference with NVIDIA Dynamo
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details NVIDIA Dynamo's full-stack optimizations for agentic inference workloads, focusing on KV cache reuse, agent-aware routing, and distributed cache management to address the unique write-once-read-many access patterns of coding agents.
